page: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is driven by a 64-bit AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance configuration allocates two virtual CPUs backed by a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe or solid-state storage, necessitating remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps with zero included public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements reflect the profile of a dual-thread single-core allocation. In compute evaluations, the m6a.large attains strong single-core execution in stress-ng with a score of 2989.08, placing in the top quartile. However, aggregate multi-core and throughput testing highlights physical hardware constraints: Geekbench multi-core registers at 2009.0 and Clang compilation scores 2165.0, placing in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth assessments show 31.17 GB/s read and 21.04 GB/s write performance on 256 MB blocks, accompanied by a PassMark memory score of 1055.35. In-memory data access via Redis SET operations achieved 2.32 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 2.84 GB/s.

From an architectural standpoint, the m6a.large provides cost-efficient baseline throughput for scenarios that do not demand extensive core parallelism or local high-IOPS storage arrays. Its single physical core and shared-core threading introduce latency risks when handling heavy concurrent queues, rendering it inefficient for compute-dense parallel tasks or heavy database clusters. It is well suited for small-scale web serving, microservices, continuous integration testing agents, basic background worker queues, and general-purpose development environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine configured on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features two vCPUs mapped to one physical core on an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz, along with 8.0 GB of DDR4 system memory operating at 3 GHz. It carries no bundled local storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the m6a.large demonstrates strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng testing, ranking in the top tier, while multi-core metrics reflect the inherent physical constraint of having a single underlying core. Memory bandwidth and multi-threaded throughput scale moderately, matching its lightweight profile. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio delivers reliable resource density for standard operational duties. This hardware configuration is appropriate for light web serving, small-scale microservices, background task workers, test environments, and foundational business applications with modest concurrency demands.
